newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH COALITION PARTY CALLS FOR '98 VAT CUT - AGENCY.
newsitem.headline: CZECH COALITION PARTY CALLS FOR '98 VAT CUT - AGENCY.

text.p: Junior Czech coalition party, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), is demanding a cut in the value added tax (VAT) in 1998 in return for supporting a VAT hike on energy this year, the news agency CTK said on Friday.
CTK quoted ODA vice chairman and Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy as saying the regular VAT rate, which currently stands at 22 percent, should be lowered by a number of percentage points.
Dlouhy added that further discussion was needed on the extent of an overall VAT decrease in 1998.

Earlier on Friday, Dlouhy's spokesman said that the three parties which form the governing coalition have agreed to hike the VAT energies to 22 percent in July from the current five percent as a price deregulation measure.
The process should gradually eliminate the disproportionate gap between lower household and higher industrial prices.
The coalition is scheduled to meet next Wednesday to give a final appproval to the VAT increase plan.
